reference_profile.runner: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest standard runner (x86_64, 4 vCPU, 16 GB)
reference_profile.why: The one machine class every release is measured on, so two releases' numbers compare. A developer laptop is faster and noisier; the profile is what the budget means.

sustained: A breach blocks only if a second full pass reproduces it: one slow sample on a shared runner is the machine, the same breach twice is the code.

cli check.why: One spec screened in a fresh process. No progress line, so it must finish within the 2 s responsiveness threshold.

cli build.why: Cold kernel import plus a STEP write; reports progress, so it may exceed the threshold.

cli view.why: Build plus four rendered views; reports progress.

cli parts.why: The element catalog printed in a fresh process; no geometry, so within the threshold.

cli read.why: One STEP file measured in a fresh process, which pays the kernel import.

cli combine.why: Two parts built, placed and intersected in a fresh process, with the kernel import.

mcp initialize.why: Server start to the initialize reply: the wait before an agent can use any tool.

mcp build_part.why: First build pays the kernel import.

mcp render_viewport.why: One SVG view of a built part.

mcp measure_geometry.why: One measurement of a built part.

mcp export_artifact.why: The evidence bundle for a stored card.

mcp build_combination.why: Two parts built, placed and intersected; the first geometry call of a session also pays the kernel import.

mcp list_context.why: A folder's engineering files, classified by name; nothing is opened.

mcp read_cad_file.why: One CAD file measured; a STEP read pays the kernel import when it is the first geometry call.

mcp describe_part.why: One element's fields and its example spec, read before a spec is written.

time_to_first_part.why: openspec/specs/onboarding: a fresh install to an exported validated sample part in under 10 minutes.
